# Security Baseline -- Every Azure Stack Needs This

**Version**: 1.0
**Date**: 2026-03-18
**Applies to**: All infrastructure generated by the infrastructure generator
**Source**: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) v1, Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)

---

> This document defines the **minimum security controls** that every Azure deployment
> must implement. These controls are non-negotiable -- they apply regardless of tier
> (basic, standard, or premium) unless explicitly noted otherwise.

## 1. Network Security

### 1.1 Virtual Network + Subnet Isolation

Every workload runs inside a dedicated VNet with purpose-specific subnets. No resource
is deployed on a flat, shared network.

**MCSB Control**: NS-1 (Network segmentation)

```hcl
# networking.tf
module "vnet" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-network-virtualnetwork/azurerm"
  version = "~> 0.7"

  name                = "vnet-${local.name_prefix}"
  resource_group_name = module.resource_group.name
  location            = var.location
  address_space       = [var.vnet_address_space]
  enable_telemetry    = false

  subnets = {
    app = {
      name             = "snet-app-${local.name_prefix}"
      address_prefixes = [var.subnet_app_cidr]
    }
    data = {
      name             = "snet-data-${local.name_prefix}"
      address_prefixes = [var.subnet_data_cidr]
    }
    private_endpoints = {
      name             = "snet-pe-${local.name_prefix}"
      address_prefixes = [var.subnet_pe_cidr]
    }
  }
}
```

### 1.2 Network Security Groups (NSG)

Every subnet gets an NSG with a deny-all inbound default. Only required ports are opened.

**MCSB Control**: NS-1 (Network segmentation)

```hcl
# networking.tf
module "nsg_app" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-network-networksecuritygroup/azurerm"
  version = "~> 0.4"

  name                = "nsg-app-${local.name_prefix}"
  resource_group_name = module.resource_group.name
  location            = var.location
  enable_telemetry    = false

  security_rules = {
    allow_https_inbound = {
      name                       = "Allow-HTTPS-Inbound"
      priority                   = 100
      direction                  = "Inbound"
      access                     = "Allow"
      protocol                   = "Tcp"
      source_port_range          = "*"
      destination_port_range     = "443"
      source_address_prefix      = "VirtualNetwork"
      destination_address_prefix = "*"
    }
    deny_all_inbound = {
      name                       = "Deny-All-Inbound"
      priority                   = 4096
      direction                  = "Inbound"
      access                     = "Deny"
      protocol                   = "*"
      source_port_range          = "*"
      destination_port_range     = "*"
      source_address_prefix      = "*"
      destination_address_prefix = "*"
    }
  }
}
```

### 1.3 Private Endpoints

All PaaS services (databases, Key Vault, Storage, etc.) must be accessed through Private
Endpoints in standard and premium tiers. Public network access is disabled.

**MCSB Control**: NS-2 (Secure cloud services with network controls)

> **Important**: NS-2 is about Private Endpoints and disabling public access.
> Do NOT confuse with NS-3 (Firewall). These are distinct controls.

```hcl
# networking.tf
module "pe_keyvault" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-network-privateendpoint/azurerm"
  version = "~> 0.1"

  name                          = "pe-kv-${local.name_prefix}"
  location                      = var.location
  resource_group_name           = module.resource_group.name
  subnet_resource_id            = module.vnet.subnets["private_endpoints"].resource_id
  enable_telemetry              = false

  private_connection_resource_id = module.keyvault.resource_id
  subresource_names              = ["vault"]

  private_dns_zone_group = {
    zone_ids = [module.dns_zone_keyvault.resource_id]
  }
}
```

**Disabling public access** (mandatory for standard/premium tiers):

```hcl
# On Key Vault
public_network_access_enabled = var.tier == "basic" ? true : false

# On Storage Account
public_network_access_enabled = var.tier == "basic" ? true : false

# On PostgreSQL
public_network_access_enabled = var.tier == "basic" ? true : false
```

### 1.4 TLS 1.2 Minimum

Every resource that accepts network connections must enforce TLS 1.2 or higher.

**MCSB Control**: DP-3 (Encrypt sensitive data in transit)

```hcl
# PostgreSQL
module "postgresql" {
  # ...
  ssl_enforcement_enabled          = true
  ssl_minimal_tls_version_enforced = "TLS1_2"
}

# Storage Account
module "storage" {
  # ...
  min_tls_version = "TLS1_2"
}

# App Service
module "app_service" {
  # ...
  site_config = {
    minimum_tls_version = "1.2"
    ftps_state          = "Disabled"  # FTP is never acceptable
  }
}
```

## 2. Identity and Access

### 2.1 User-Assigned Managed Identity

Every resource that supports Managed Identity must use one. User-Assigned is preferred
over System-Assigned for lifecycle independence.

**MCSB Control**: IM-3 (Manage application identities securely)

```hcl
# identity.tf
module "managed_identity" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-managedidentity-userassignedidentity/azurerm"
  version = "~> 0.3"

  name                = "id-${local.name_prefix}"
  resource_group_name = module.resource_group.name
  location            = var.location
  enable_telemetry    = false
}
```

Attach to resources:

```hcl
# On App Service
identity {
  type         = "UserAssigned"
  identity_ids = [module.managed_identity.resource_id]
}

# On Key Vault access
role_assignments = {
  mi_secrets = {
    role_definition_id_or_name = "Key Vault Secrets User"
    principal_id               = module.managed_identity.principal_id
  }
}
```

### 2.2 No Credentials in Code

Passwords, connection strings, API keys -- none of these belong in Terraform code or
`terraform.tfvars`. Passwords are generated randomly and stored in Key Vault.

**MCSB Control**: IM-3 (Manage application identities securely)

**Rules**:

| What | Allowed | Forbidden |
|------|---------|-----------|
| Database admin password | `random_password` + Key Vault secret | Hardcoded string |
| Storage access key | Managed Identity RBAC | Shared key in app config |
| API keys | Key Vault reference | Environment variable in code |
| Container Registry auth | Managed Identity | `admin_enabled = true` |
| Service Bus auth | Managed Identity + RBAC | `local_auth_enabled = true` |

### 2.3 No Admin Enabled on ACR

Container Registry must never have the admin account enabled. Use Managed Identity
and AcrPull/AcrPush roles instead.

```hcl
# CORRECT
module "acr" {
  # ...
  admin_enabled = false

  role_assignments = {
    aks_pull = {
      role_definition_id_or_name = "AcrPull"
      principal_id               = module.aks_identity.principal_id
    }
  }
}

# FORBIDDEN -- will fail Checkov CKV_AZURE_137
module "acr" {
  # ...
  admin_enabled = true  # NEVER
}
```

### 2.4 RBAC with Least Privilege

Role assignments follow the principle of least privilege. No `Owner` or `Contributor`
at the resource group level unless strictly necessary and documented.

**MCSB Control**: PA-7 (Follow just enough administration principle)

```hcl
# identity.tf -- grant only what's needed
role_assignments = {
  mi_storage_blob = {
    role_definition_id_or_name = "Storage Blob Data Reader"  # Not Contributor
    principal_id               = module.managed_identity.principal_id
    scope                      = module.storage.resource_id
  }
}
```

## 3. Encryption

### 3.1 Encryption at Rest

All data at rest must be encrypted. Platform-managed keys (PMK) are the minimum.
Customer-managed keys (CMK) are available in premium tier.

**MCSB Control**: DP-4 (Enable data at rest encryption by default)

| Resource | Default Encryption | CMK Support |
|----------|-------------------|-------------|
| Storage Account | AES-256 (PMK) | Yes, via Key Vault |
| SQL Database | TDE (PMK) | Yes, via Key Vault |
| PostgreSQL Flexible | AES-256 (PMK) | Yes, via Key Vault |
| Key Vault | HSM-backed (PMK) | Yes (Managed HSM) |
| Cosmos DB | AES-256 (PMK) | Yes, via Key Vault |
| Managed Disks | AES-256 (PMK) | Yes, via DES |

### 3.2 Encryption in Transit

TLS 1.2 is enforced everywhere (see section 1.4). Additionally:

**MCSB Control**: DP-3 (Encrypt sensitive data in transit)

```hcl
# Storage Account -- HTTPS only
module "storage" {
  # ...
  https_traffic_only_enabled = true
}

# Redis Cache -- no non-SSL port
module "redis" {
  # ...
  enable_non_ssl_port = false
  minimum_tls_version = "1.2"
}
```

### 3.3 Key Vault Hardening

Key Vault is the central secrets store. It must be hardened with purge protection
and soft delete.

**MCSB Controls**: DP-6 (Use a secure key management process), DP-8 (Ensure security of key and certificate repository)

```hcl
# keyvault.tf
module "keyvault" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-keyvault-vault/azurerm"
  version = "~> 0.9"

  name                       = "kv-${local.name_prefix}"
  resource_group_name        = module.resource_group.name
  location                   = var.location
  tenant_id                  = data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
  enable_telemetry           = false

  purge_protection_enabled   = true
  soft_delete_retention_days = 90

  enable_rbac_authorization  = true
  sku_name                   = "standard"

  network_acls = var.tier != "basic" ? {
    default_action = "Deny"
    bypass         = "AzureServices"
    ip_rules       = []
    virtual_network_subnet_ids = [
      module.vnet.subnets["app"].resource_id
    ]
  } : null

  public_network_access_enabled = var.tier == "basic" ? true : false
}
```

## 4. Secrets Management

### 4.1 Random Password Generation

Database passwords and other secrets are generated using `random_password` and
immediately stored in Key Vault. They never appear in plan output or state in
cleartext.

```hcl
# keyvault.tf
resource "random_password" "db_admin" {
  length           = 32
  special          = true
  override_special = "!@#$%"
  min_upper        = 2
  min_lower        = 2
  min_numeric      = 2
  min_special      = 2
}

module "keyvault" {
  # ... (module config above)

  secrets = {
    db-admin-password = {
      value = random_password.db_admin.result
    }
  }

  secrets_value = {} # Use secrets block, not secrets_value
}
```

### 4.2 Reference Pattern

Application code retrieves secrets from Key Vault at runtime via Managed Identity --
never from environment variables containing the actual secret value.

```hcl
# app.tf -- App Service with Key Vault reference
module "app_service" {
  # ...
  app_settings = {
    # Key Vault reference -- the app reads from KV at runtime
    "DB_CONNECTION_STRING" = "@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=${module.keyvault.resource_id}/secrets/db-connection-string)"

    # NEVER this:
    # "DB_PASSWORD" = random_password.db_admin.result  # FORBIDDEN
  }
}
```

## 5. Checkov Enforcement

Every stack includes a `.checkov.yaml` file. All skips must be documented with
justification.

### 5.1 Allowed Global Skips

```yaml
# .checkov.yaml
soft-fail: false
compact: true
framework:
  - terraform

skip-check:
  # AVM modules are sourced from Terraform Registry, not Git
  - CKV_TF_1

  # App Service PME: these controls require ASE which is not
  # cost-effective for PME/SMB tier deployments
  - CKV_AZURE_225  # ASE deployment
  - CKV_AZURE_211  # ASE v3
  - CKV_AZURE_212  # ASE v3
```

### 5.2 Skip Policy

| Rule | Allowed? | Condition |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Silent skip (no justification) | **NEVER** | -- |
| Skip with justification | Yes | Must document reason + alternative |
| Skip for PME cost reasons | Yes | Must document + note tier where control is active |
| Skip for brownfield targets | Yes | CI only, must document |

## 6. MCSB Control Mapping Summary

| Security Domain | Control | What It Covers | Implementation |
|----------------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Network | NS-1 | Network segmentation | VNet + subnets + NSG |
| Network | NS-2 | Secure cloud services | Private Endpoints + disable public access |
| Network | NS-3 | Edge firewall | Azure Firewall + UDR (standard/premium) |
| Identity | IM-3 | App identity management | User-Assigned Managed Identity |
| Access | PA-7 | Least privilege | Scoped RBAC, no Owner |
| Data | DP-3 | Encryption in transit | TLS 1.2+, HTTPS only |
| Data | DP-4 | Encryption at rest | Platform-managed keys (minimum) |
| Data | DP-6 | Key management | Key Vault with RBAC |
| Data | DP-8 | Key repository security | Purge protection + soft delete 90d |
